title: Triggered fallback and graceful regression policy for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: define a machine-actionable policy and PRD for triggered fallbacks and graduated rollbacks when Optimize detects quality regressions. The policy must tie together promptset sampling, multi-signal regression detection (quality delta, safety/hallucination signals, latency/cost), A/B testing rules, and an automated canary gate that supports both automatic mitigation and operator override. This ticket produces the acceptance criteria, measurement plan, and rollout choreography for the initial implementation (v1) that covers hosted API and Dedicated deployments.
background: We currently run promptset evaluations in Optimize that surface regressions, but team-level responses are manual and inconsistent. Customers and SREs want a predictable, auditable path from detection to remediation that avoids unnecessary full rollbacks while protecting user-facing quality. This PRD aligns product, runtime, and SRE on a deterministic policy that lives in the control plane and emits clear actions (no-op, traffic-shape to fallback model, full rollback, or trigger retrain job).
scope: In scope: definition of signals, thresholds, A/B criteria, canary traffic schedule, automatic mitigation actions (model fallback, per-route traffic split), alerting, and audit logs. Out of scope: automatic model retraining (only a placeholder action) and cross-region routing changes for v1.
scope_changes: Added per-customer cohort support after stakeholder review (2026-03-03): canaries must be runnable against customer cohorts with separate baseline metrics. This increases evaluation sample sets by ~20% and requires metadata tagging in samples. Also added an explicit low-latency exception rule for latency-sensitive enterprise routes.
metrics_and_thresholds:
Primary signals and v1 thresholds (configurable):
- Quality delta: rolling 24h cohort-level mean quality score drop >= 2.0 percentage points (relative) -> signal.
- Safety/Hallucination: hallucination-rate (proxy via NER-based hallucination heuristic) increase >= 0.4 percentage points -> signal.
- Latency regression: P95 latency increase >= 15% AND absolute P95 > 350ms for hosted API -> signal.
- Cost-per-token: unit cost increase >= 12% -> advisory signal.
Rollback decision: require 2 independent signals OR single high-severity signal (quality delta >= 5.0 pp OR safety increase >= 1.0 pp). All signals must be sustained for at least 30 minutes and statistically significant at p<0.05 (see A/B criteria).
promptset_and_sampling:
Promptset composition and sampling cadence:
- Baseline promptset size: 5k stratified samples per major cohort (web search, chat, embeddings, re-ranking).
- Edge-case bucket: 500 synthetic adversarial prompts selected by fuzzing / historical false-positive triggers.
- Sampling cadence: continuous streaming evaluation with daily batch aggregation; sentinel runs every 6 hours for canary gates.
- Stratification keys: customer_cohort, route_type, token_length_bucket, locale.
- Retention for comparisons: last 14 days of aggregated prompt results for trend analysis.
a_b_criteria_and_stat_tests:
A/B test design for changes that might affect quality:
- Minimum sample size per arm: 2,000 prompts per cohort for primary metric to ensure power > 0.8 for a 2pp lift.
- Significance: two-sided t-test with sequential correction (alpha-spending using O'Brien-Fleming) and minimum runtime of 24 hours.
- Stopping rules: stop early for superiority if p<0.001 and effect size > 3pp; stop for harm on pre-specified early-warning signals (see metrics_and_thresholds).
- Multiple comparisons: adjust using Benjamini-Hochberg when evaluating >4 metrics concurrently.
- Confidence intervals and Bayesian posterior estimates must be published by the evaluation job for transparency.
rollback_triggers_and_mitigation_actions:
Automated mitigation actions ordered by severity and reversibility:
1) Soft fallback: shift 20% traffic to the previous stable model variant for 30 minutes (auto-heal if signals subside).
2) Progressive traffic-shape: increase fallback by 20pp every 30 minutes up to 100% unless stopped manually.
3) Full rollback: switch routing to pinned previous version and mark release as 'rolled back' in audit log.
4) Retrain trigger: create flagged action for ML team with attached failing promptset snapshot (manual review required).
Auto-trigger logic: require multi-signal rule (2 of 3 or single high-severity). All automated actions write an immutable audit event and send paged alert to SRE on-call if customer_impact == high.
rollout_plan:
Canary choreography for model updates under Optimize:
- Step 0: Preflight sentinel run against full baseline promptset (5k) and pass all soft checks.
- Step 1: 1% traffic canary for 60 minutes. Evaluate sentinel runs; if no signals, proceed.
- Step 2: 10% traffic for 3 hours with sentinel every 6 hours.
- Step 3: 40% traffic for 6 hours.
- Step 4: 100% ramp if all signals within thresholds for 24h.
- Hold windows: any failing signal stops the rollout and executes mitigation per rollback_triggers. Manual overrides require two approvers (PM + Eng).
test_plan: Pre-merge: unit tests for signal detection logic, integration tests for canary traffic-shape API, synthetic regression simulations. Staging: run 3 simulated rollouts using historical regression events; compare policy decisions to the historical corrective action. Prod: parallel shadowing enabled for first two production rollouts; operator signoff required before automated mitigation enabled.
acceptance_criteria:
Must-have acceptance criteria for v1:
- Policy engine can evaluate the multi-signal rule and emit an action within 60s of sustained signal window.
- Sentinel evaluation pipeline produces aggregated metrics and p-values to the dashboard and is queryable via API.
- Canary workflow supports 1%, 10%, 40%, 100% ramps with automated traffic-shape and rollback actions.
- Audit logs show deterministic decision tree path for every triggered action and link to failing promptset snapshot.
- 3 simulated regressions in staging must result in expected mitigation (soft fallback or rollback) in >=90% of scenarios.
- Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with runbook steps and escalation matrix.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risks: false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks; underpowered sample sizes for small cohorts; latency-sensitive routes misclassified.
Mitigations: require multi-signal confirmation for automated rollback, implement minimum sample constraint per cohort, and add explicit low-latency exception routes that only trigger advisory alerts instead of automated fallbacks.
